slides.title: URL Shortener Overview
content: A URL shortener converts long URLs into short unique aliases
Allows users to access original URLs using shortened links
Designed for high scalability and availability
Handles massive number of requests efficiently
Used in platforms like social media and messaging apps

slides.title: Core Use Cases
content: Shortening long URLs into compact links
Redirecting users from short URL to original URL
Handling high traffic with low latency
Ensuring high availability and reliability
Supporting scalable distributed systems

slides.title: System Estimation
content: System may handle around 100 million URLs per day
Total URLs can reach billions over years
Uses 62 characters including digits and alphabets
Short URL length of 6 to 7 characters is sufficient
Helps estimate storage and scalability requirements

slides.title: API Design
content: POST endpoint is used to create short URLs
GET endpoint is used to redirect to original URL
Uses HTTP 301 redirect for permanent redirection
APIs are stateless for scalability
Requires validation for invalid or malicious URLs

slides.title: Data Model
content: Stores mapping between short URL and long URL
Uses unique ID as primary key
Short URL is indexed for fast lookup
Long URL stored as text
System is append-only and continuously grows

slides.title: Hashing Approach
content: Hash functions convert long URLs into short identifiers
Methods include MD5 or SHA hashing
Collisions must be handled explicitly
May require multiple database checks
Less efficient for large-scale systems

slides.title: Base62 Encoding
content: Converts numeric ID into short string using 62 characters
Ensures no collision when used with unique IDs
Produces compact and readable URLs
Deterministic and fast conversion
Preferred method in large-scale systems

slides.title: URL Shortening Flow
content: System receives long URL from user
Checks if URL already exists
Generates unique ID
Converts ID into Base62 string
Stores mapping in database and returns short URL

slides.title: URL Redirecting Flow
content: User accesses short URL
Request is routed through load balancer
System checks cache for mapping
If cache miss occurs, fetch from database
Returns HTTP redirect response to original URL

slides.title: Caching Strategy
content: Uses cache-aside pattern for performance
Frequently accessed URLs stored in memory
LRU policy used for eviction
TTL defines cache expiration time
Database acts as source of truth

slides.title: Performance Benefits
content: Caching reduces database load significantly
Provides millisecond-level response time
Handles high read traffic efficiently
Improves user experience with faster redirects
Scales easily for large number of requests

slides.title: System Challenges
content: Cache consistency issues may arise
Storage grows continuously over time
Requires database sharding at scale
Handling duplicate URLs efficiently is needed
Requires proper monitoring and maintenance

slides.title: Scalability Techniques
content: Database sharding distributes data across servers
Replication improves read performance and availability
Load balancing distributes incoming traffic
Stateless servers allow horizontal scaling
System avoids single point of failure

slides.title: Additional Features
content: Rate limiting prevents abuse of system
Analytics tracks click counts and usage patterns
Monitoring ensures system reliability
Security prevents malicious URLs
Logging helps debugging and performance tuning

slides.title: Important Concepts
content: Unique ID generator creates globally unique identifiers
Base62 encoding converts numbers into short strings
Cache-aside loads data from DB on cache miss
TTL defines how long cache data is valid
Sharding distributes data horizontally
Replication copies data for availability

slides.title: Final Summary
content: URL shortener systems map long URLs to short identifiers
Base62 encoding with unique ID generation is preferred approach
Caching ensures fast redirection performance
Database design supports scalability and persistence
System handles billions of requests efficiently
